expectations.text: Identifies the request as too large for a single issue and proposes splitting
expectations.evidence: Step 2 explicitly states 'This idea clearly needs decomposition' and provides 4 bullet points explaining why: multiple independent user-facing outcomes, different subsystems, natural shipping boundaries, acceptance criteria span unrelated areas.

expectations.text: Decomposes into 2-4 separate issues with clear boundaries
expectations.evidence: Decomposed into 5 issues (core infrastructure, in-app UI, email delivery, user preferences, admin templates). While boundaries are clear and well-defined, 5 exceeds the 2-4 range. The decomposition separated email delivery and user preferences into distinct issues, where the baseline combined them.

expectations.text: Each decomposed issue has its own Job Story, Promise, and Acceptance Criteria
expectations.evidence: All 5 issues have complete Job Story (When/I want/so I can format), Promise, Constraints, and Acceptance Criteria sections. Each is self-contained with 8-11 acceptance criteria per issue.

expectations.text: Shows dependency relationships between the decomposed issues
expectations.evidence: Includes a dependency table (# | Issue | Depends On | Rationale), an ASCII dependency graph, recommended implementation order with parallelization notes, and pipeline mode recommendations per issue.

expectations.text: Notification preferences/configuration is separated from the core notification infrastructure
expectations.evidence: Issue #4 (User notification preferences) is a dedicated issue, completely separate from Issue #1 (Core notification infrastructure). Depends on #1, #2, and #3 as prerequisites.

expectations.text: Admin panel is a separate issue from user-facing notifications
expectations.evidence: Issue #5 (Admin notification template management) is a dedicated issue separate from Issues #2 and #3 (user-facing). Depends on #1 and #3 only.

expectations.text: Presents all issues for user confirmation before creating any
expectations.evidence: Step 4 presents all issues with dependency graph and implementation order. Step 5 shows all 5 acorn issue create commands labeled 'DRY RUN — NOT EXECUTED', with post-creation steps noting to update cross-references after user confirms.
